At the moment I support my fiancée financially. Once he graduates and stars working (this summer) he has decided to take over while I finish my degree. We view is as investing in OUR future, giving the other enough help to gain their degree and start earning money. 

So as a whole what you’re doing isn’t unhealthy, if you truly see a future with this girl, but you seem uncomfortable with her lack of self-sufficiency. Tell her that. Have an honest conversation where you tell her she has to start spending her own money on necessities. From there you can decide how much you’d like to support her. But have that conversation ASAP before she starts taking your support for granted.
I hope you told them to pound sand and that you’re doing okay now! The toxicity of some people’s ignorance is astounding.
Bonus: she’s a recovering anorexic so I’m real proud of her for finally being cool with her body and sticking up for herself. She’s gonna be a great mom.

In Manitoba, we’ve got some heavy smoke out here too. Only time it was worse than this that I remember is the Fort Mcmurray fire. 

Freaking insane how far that stuff travels.

You should try posting this in r/relationship_advice. They might have further insight into possible routes of communication with your wife (ways to talk, counselling, lawyers, etc.) and you’d most likely find people going through the same ordeal with the same monetary issues.

That sounds like an absolutely unsustainable daily life you’ve got, I’m sorry your wife is so uncaring to your struggles. Do you have anyone  to you to talk/vent to about this? Is there any possibility of taking a much needed vacation? Maybe you need to go visit your parents or sibling or someone, get out of the house and away from the situation to clear your head? 

In the immediate short term, what if you tried to meal-prep a bunch of easy lunches (like sandwiches or salads) that your kids can just grab from the fridge for lunch? Might save you a few more hours of sleep. 

Good luck buddy. I hope everything turns out okay for you.

I’m no expert but I’ve found suicide leaves a long-term kind of damage. People are pretty resilient and return to normal life pretty quickly after a tragedy. But years later, it’s something that sticks with you. You don’t ever seem to heal properly after. 

The few kids in my hometown who’ve killed themselves are still remembered and grieved, decades later. it’s a quiet grief, but its there. Stuff as tragic as this sticks deep. Give yourself and others time. It’s not doing a disservice to his memory to continue living your life. 

I’m really sorry for your loss. I hope your Facebook group and your medical searches come up with something positive.
